(i) we introduce the first practical black box adversarial attack against DNNs, (ii) it is effective in the real world, (iii) it works for a wide variety of ML techniques, (iv) it can evade defenses, and (v) it is easy to implement and execute.
We introduce the first black box attack strategy against deep neural networks.
we have demonstrated the first practical black box adversarial example attack against a remotely hosted machine learning system.

the practicality of adversarial examples in the real world.
the practicality of black box attacks against DNNs.
the practicality of adversarial example attacks against remotely hosted ML systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our black-box attack strategy against DNNs is the first to be practical, and is capable of evasive behavior against defense strategies.
the black box attack strategy presented in this paper is the most practical and effective attack against deep neural networks.
our attack is a proof of concept of the possibility to attack a remotely hosted Dnn with no knowledge of the Dnn internals or its training set, which is the most realistic scenario.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, given a DNN, we can find a local substitute model which is able to craft adversarial example that will mislead the target DNN with a very high success rate.
the black-box attack is practical and effective, and it can bypass the defense strategies.
our black box attack is practical and effective.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ML models can be attacked without knowledge of their internals or training data, and that this is not only a theoretical possibility but a practical threat.
ML is vulnerable to black box attacks, and that the only information an adversary requires to perform such an attack is the label of chosen inputs.
ML systems can be attacked without access to the model or training data, and that the threat of adversarial examples is not limited to DNNs.
